HOME_PAGE.DELIVER_TEXT: With your submission approved, your administrator delivers it to your institution's repository, and to ProQuest. As with any other content available on the ProQuest platform, work needs to be done before your dissertation or thesis can be made discoverable on ProQuest. The average time it takes to do this work is 4–6 weeks. When the work is complete, your dissertation or thesis is ready to be made available on ProQuest. Any embargo period you specified will be enforced when your work is on ProQuest.

HOME_PAGE.DONE_TEXT: ProQuest staff ensure formatting and details about your work are correct before uploading it and making it discoverable in ProQuest. HOME_PAGE.REVIEW_TEXT: The ETD administrator at your institution reviews your submission. Typically, administrators will be checking to make sure your submission includes all of the information required by your institution. Institutions often enforce their own style and formatting standards, so they'll also be looking to make sure your submission adheres to those standards.
HOME_PAGE.REVISE_APPROVE_TEXT: After reviewing your submission, your institutional administrator will inform you of any necessary revisions. You make the revisions and upload the changes to your existing submission. When no more revisions are needed, the administrator approves your submission. The next step will be to deliver it to your institution's repository, and to ProQuest, within applicable policies and timelines enforced by your institution.

PAPER.ABSTRACT_TEXT: Excessive alcohol consumption poses significant risks to liver health, manifesting in a range of histopathological changes. Among these, one prominent outcome is the development of steatosis, commonly known as fatty liver disease. This condition emerges when the liver accumulates excessive fat, leading to inflammation and compromised liver function. Moreover, chronic alcohol abuse can precipitate the onset of alcoholic hepatitis, an inflammatory condition of the liver that spans a spectrum of severity. Symptoms may include jaundice, abdominal pain, and in severe cases, liver failure. Alcoholic hepatitis represents a critical juncture in the progression of alcohol-related liver diseases, often signaling the potential for irreversible damage.
